The line anchors below are resolved against this staged vulnerable tree because it matches the saved AddressSanitizer frames at `H5Fint.c:2859`, `H5Gent.c:148`, and `H5Fsuper_cache.c:521`.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42520210 (hdf5): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target h5_read_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42520210
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / reproduction_report.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source in `_work/src/hdf5` / staged harness `_work/src/h5_read_fuzzer.c` / staged `poc`
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged 149-byte fuzz input with SHA-256 `6363ecdcc35ed91be0c6faf722e3879d48394f3f291654a4a0d4d8910f080a2a` is not parsed by HDF5 directly: `_work/src/h5_read_fuzzer.c` stores byte 0 in `decider`, strips that byte, and writes only bytes 1..148 to the temp file later opened with `H5Fopen()`. In that 148-byte temp file, bytes 0-7 are the HDF5 signature, byte 8 decodes to `super_vers == 1`, and legacy prefix bytes 13 and 14 decode to `sizeof_addr == 16` and `sizeof_size == 32`. `H5F__cache_superblock_get_final_load_size()` turns those attacker-controlled widths into `actual_len == 164`, so `H5C__load_entry()` reallocates the heap-backed superblock image to the 164-byte region later named by AddressSanitizer. `H5F__cache_superblock_deserialize()` then re-runs `H5F__superblock_prefix_decode()` on that reallocated image, re-materializes the same legacy width fields into file state, advances over four 16-byte addresses, and reaches `H5G_ent_decode()` with the root-entry cache-type word `tmp == 1` (`H5G_CACHED_STAB`) from temp-file bytes 140-143. The fixed `H5G_SIZEOF_SCRATCH == 16` root-entry scratch area begins at image offset 148 of the 164-byte superblock buffer, but the STAB arm decodes two 16-byte addresses from it without any remaining-length check. The first decode consumes bytes 148-163 of the heap image, and the second `H5F_addr_decode()` enters `H5F_addr_decode_len()` at `src/H5Fint.c:2859`, where `c = *(*pp)++;` reads one byte past the end of that 164-byte allocation and reproduces the saved AddressSanitizer `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1`. The patch fixes the witnessed path by threading `image_end`/`p_end` through superblock and root-entry decoding and rejecting buffer overflows with `H5_IS_BUFFER_OVERFLOW(...)` before the vulnerable reads.

source.description: Source. This is the first project-code statement that materializes vulnerability-relevant state from the temp-file image written by the harness. On the exact witness it reads legacy superblock version `1`, the dispatch key for the vulnerable old-format decode path.
source.value_from: The staged 149-byte `poc` with SHA-256 `6363ecdcc35ed91be0c6faf722e3879d48394f3f291654a4a0d4d8910f080a2a` is not parsed directly. `_work/src/h5_read_fuzzer.c:20-31` stores byte 0 in `decider`, then writes only bytes 1..148 to the temp file passed to `H5Fopen()`. In that 148-byte temp file, bytes 0-7 are the HDF5 signature and byte 8 (fuzz offset 9) is `0x01`, so this statement materializes `super_vers == 1` from the temp-file image.
source.note: The libFuzzer entry is the unscored harness boundary. The vulnerability-relevant parser state starts here, after the harness has stripped the one-byte prefix from the staged fuzz input.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: Root cause. In the `H5G_CACHED_STAB` arm, vulnerable code decodes two `H5F_SIZEOF_ADDR(f)`-byte cached addresses from the root-entry scratch pad without checking whether that much space remains. On the witnessed path `pp` enters the scratch area at image offset 148, `H5F_SIZEOF_ADDR(f) == 16`, and the block demands 32 bytes from the fixed `H5G_SIZEOF_SCRATCH == 16` extent.
root_cause.note: The adjacent `HDassert(2 * H5F_SIZEOF_ADDR(f) <= H5G_SIZEOF_SCRATCH)` records the intended invariant but is not a release-build guard. The patch threads `p_end` down to this function and inserts `H5_IS_BUFFER_OVERFLOW(*pp, H5F_SIZEOF_ADDR(f) * 2, p_end)` immediately before these two decodes.

sink.description: ASan crash site. `H5F_addr_decode_len()` blindly reads the next byte of an address from `*pp`. On the second cached-STAB address decode, that byte read lands just past the heap-backed 164-byte superblock image.
sink.note: AddressSanitizer reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at this exact line and says the faulting address is `0 bytes to the right of 164-byte region [0x60f000000040,0x60f0000000e4)` allocated for the superblock image.

parser_admitted.description: After the second deserialize-pass prefix decode has accepted the temp-file image, deserialization enters the legacy superblock parser because the re-materialized version byte is `< 2`.
parser_admitted.note: On the exact witness the second pass again yields `super_vers == 1`, so this old-format branch is the control gate that makes root group symbol-table entry decoding reachable.

tainted_value_origin.description: The legacy superblock prefix materializes the attacker-controlled width fields that drive both the final superblock allocation size and the later address/length decode widths. On the exact witness this block yields `sizeof_addr == 16` and `sizeof_size == 32`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: After the harness strips fuzz byte 0 and HDF5 skips the signature plus version byte, the legacy prefix bytes at temp-file offsets 13 and 14 (fuzz offsets 14 and 15) are `0x10` and `0x20`. This statement therefore materializes `sizeof_addr == 16` and `sizeof_size == 32` from the 148-byte temp-file image, not from the raw 149-byte staged input parsed directly.
tainted_value_origin.note: `sizeof_addr` is the critical width: once the deserialize pass copies it into `udata->f->shared->sizeof_addr`, every downstream `H5F_addr_decode()` consumes 16 bytes, including the two cached-STAB reads that outrun the fixed 16-byte scratch field.

fine_trace.note: The staged witness begins with `0x20`. The harness stores that byte in `decider`, decrements `size` to 148, advances `data` by one, and writes only the remaining 148 bytes to a temp file. Because the branch condition is `decider % 1 == 0`, that temp file is always routed to `H5Fopen()`, so HDF5 sees the signature at temp-file offset 0 even though it was at fuzz-input offset 1.

Source step. After HDF5 has located the signature at temp-file offset 0, this statement reads the next byte at temp-file offset 8. On the exact witness that byte is `0x01`, so the superblock is treated as legacy version 1.

depends_on.via: data + 1 bytes written to temp file

fine_trace.note: Because `super_vers == 1`, the old-format prefix path reads the width fields from the legacy locations. The exact witness sets `sizeof_addr == 16` from temp-file byte 13 and `sizeof_size == 32` from temp-file byte 14.

These attacker-controlled fields determine the final superblock image size. For `super_vers == 1`, `sizeof_addr == 16`, and `sizeof_size == 32`, the macro expands to a 164-byte image, including `H5G_SIZEOF_ENTRY(16, 32) == 72` bytes for the root entry with only a fixed 16-byte scratch area.

The cache loader starts from the minimal speculative superblock length (`H5F_SUPERBLOCK_FIXED_SIZE + H5F_SUPERBLOCK_MINIMAL_VARLEN_SIZE == 16`), re-runs the final-size callback, gets `actual_len == 164`, and reallocates `image` to the 164-byte heap region later reported by ASan (`[0x60f000000040,0x60f0000000e4)`).

During the deserialize call at `src/H5Fsuper_cache.c:433`, HDF5 re-runs `H5F__superblock_prefix_decode()` on the reallocated heap image. This fresh second pass again reads `super_vers == 1`; it is not direct dataflow from the first pass's temporary `sblock` in step 2.
The same second pass re-reads the legacy width bytes from the reallocated image and again materializes `sizeof_addr == 16` and `sizeof_size == 32` before control returns to the deserializer.
The actual deserialize path enters the legacy superblock parser because the second-pass version byte is still `< 2`. This is the control gate that reaches root group symbol-table entry decoding.
The second-pass width fields are copied into file state, so downstream `H5F_addr_decode()` and `H5F_DECODE_LENGTH()` calls now use 16-byte addresses and 32-byte lengths on the crashing path.

After the non-vulnerable legacy fixed fields, these four address decodes each consume `H5F_SIZEOF_ADDR(f) == 16` bytes and advance `image` from offset 28 to offset 92 of the 164-byte heap image, placing the root group symbol-table entry at image offset 92.

Root-entry header decoding consumes a 32-byte length, a 16-byte address, a 4-byte cache-type word, and 4 reserved bytes. On the witness, temp-file bytes 140-143 (fuzz offsets 141-144) decode `tmp == 1`, so `ent->type` becomes `H5G_CACHED_STAB`; `pp` then lands at root-entry scratch offset 148, which is also the end of the 148-byte temp-file image.

Root-cause step. Because `ent->type == H5G_CACHED_STAB`, this arm tries to decode two 16-byte addresses from `pp == image + 148`. The first decode consumes bytes 148-163 of the 164-byte heap image; the second begins at `image + 164`. The `HDassert` records that `2 * H5F_SIZEOF_ADDR(f)` should fit within `H5G_SIZEOF_SCRATCH == 16`, but no runtime remaining-length check enforces that invariant in the vulnerable build.

Sink step. On the second `H5F_addr_decode()` from step 12, `H5F_addr_decode_len()` executes this byte read with `*pp == image + 164`, i.e. on the first byte past the 164-byte heap-backed superblock image from step 5. AddressSanitizer reports this exact `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `src/H5Fint.c:2859`.

allocation_context.description: ASan's allocation stack shows `H5C__load_entry()` growing the heap-backed superblock image with `H5MM_realloc(image, actual_len + H5C_IMAGE_EXTRA_SPACE)` before the later out-of-bounds read.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. The trace now carries the staged fuzz input through the harness's one-byte strip into a 148-byte temp file, through `actual_len == 164` and `H5C__load_entry()`'s `H5MM_realloc(...)`, then through the second deserialize-pass width copy into the missing bounds check in `H5G_ent_decode()` that overruns that exact 164-byte image.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved ASan stack is `H5F_addr_decode_len -> H5F_addr_decode -> H5G_ent_decode -> H5F__cache_superblock_deserialize -> H5C__load_entry -> ...`, and the fine trace refines that exact path with the harness-to-temp-file mapping, the initial size computation, the second deserialize-pass prefix decode, and the root-entry offset arithmetic that set up the crash.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42520210 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the staged `poc` file to `/out/h5_read_fuzzer`. The harness stored byte 0 in `decider`, wrote only bytes 1..148 to `/tmp/libfuzzer.<pid>`, and `H5Fopen()` on that temp file reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` with stack `H5F_addr_decode_len -> H5F_addr_decode -> H5G_ent_decode`.

format.name: libFuzzer input with 1-byte decider prefix and HDF5 temp-file image
format.contract: Exactly the staged 149-byte binary file with SHA-256 `6363ecdcc35ed91be0c6faf722e3879d48394f3f291654a4a0d4d8910f080a2a`. Byte 0 is consumed by `h5_read_fuzzer` as `decider` and is not part of the HDF5 file that the library parses. The harness writes only bytes 1..148 to the temp file passed to `H5Fopen()`, so the parsed HDF5 image is exactly 148 bytes long with the signature at file offsets 0-7, `super_vers == 1` at file offset 8 (fuzz offset 9), `sizeof_addr == 16` and `sizeof_size == 32` at file offsets 13 and 14 (fuzz offsets 14 and 15), and the root-entry cache-type word `0x00000001` at file offsets 140-143 (fuzz offsets 141-144). On this exact witness the root-entry scratch area starts at image offset 148 of the 164-byte superblock buffer, so `H5G_ent_decode()`'s two 16-byte STAB address decodes exhaust that allocation and the second one overruns it. Stage 01 proves only this exact fuzz input, harness strip, and observed legacy superblock/root-entry path; this contract does not generalize to neighboring field values or other HDF5 layouts.
